title: Hybrid stochastic batch sculpting for tail-latency reduction
creator: Ava Patel
description: Goal: reduce p95/p99 tail latency spikes caused by long-tail request shapes and noisy admission bursts by introducing a hybrid stochastic batch sculpting admission controller that (1) probabilistically trims large batches when the predicted cost/latency tradeoff is unfavorable, (2) prioritizes decode-bound requests with per-request urgency scores, and (3) informs kernel selection with expected sequence-length distributions. This ticket designs and implements the controller, integrates it with prefill/decode schedulers, and validates end-to-end latency and throughput impacts on production-like workloads.
acceptance_criteria: p99 end-to-end decode latency reduced by >=20% for mixed short+long workloads compared to current admission baseline
no more than 5% regression in overall token throughput at 95% tail under synthetic burst traffic
admission controller exposes observability metrics (admit_rate, sculpt_actions, trimmed_tokens, priority_reorders) and dashboards exist
kernel-selector receives request-level expected sequence-length histogram and uses it to pick quantized kernels for >90% of cases
feature rollout plan with canary gating and auto-rollback if tail SLI degrades beyond threshold
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Spike completed — evaluated simple deterministic trimming heuristics; latency improved but throughput degraded on small requests
2026-03-11: Implemented Poisson-based probabilistic admission prototype in test harness; added per-request urgency score derived from client timeout and SLA tier
2026-03-12: Integrated urgency scores into prefill scheduler; began instrumenting sculpt_actions metric and end-to-end tracing for kernel-switch events
technical_notes: Design: Hybrid approach combines a stochastic admission policy (probability p trim depending on current batch size, queued latency, and predicted decode cost) with a deterministic fast-path for urgent short requests.

Kernel selection: Admission controller embeds expected sequence-length pmf (3-bucket: short/medium/long) as part of scheduling hints so kernel planner can choose between optimized small-seq kernels and general-purpose kernels with KV-cache tradeoffs.
Prefill/Decode coordination: When sculpting trims tokens from prefill candidates, controller marks requests for decode-priority so their KV warmups are preserved where possible.
Backpressure: Maintain request-level backoff tokens for clients to avoid thundering herd after trims; expose Retry-After header when probability of drop exceeds threshold.

Observability: Add metrics including sculpt_probability, trimmed_count_by_bucket, priority_promotions, and histogram of p99_by_model_variant. Traces should include admission_decision and kernel_choice spans.

Trade-offs: Stochastic trimming reduces worst-case batch size but introduces nondeterministic per-request latency; mitigated via urgency fast-path and SLA-aware weighting. May require customer opt-out for strict determinism.
Safety: Ensure customer-requested pinned model variants are honored; sculpting should only apply to model-variant-compatible fallbacks where allowed by customer config.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for admission probability function with boundary conditions
Integration tests simulating mixed workload (60% short, 30% medium, 10% long) with synthetic arrival bursts
A/B canary against 5% of traffic with gradual ramp to 25% and automated SLI checks (p99_latency, token_throughput)
Chaos test: simulate delayed KV cache population and verify sculpting prevents cascade latencies
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal canary on sandbox cluster with recorded production traces replay (1 week)
Phase 1: Canary on 2% of low-risk customer traffic with tight SLI monitoring (72h)
Phase 2: Ramp to 25% if SLI pass; collect kernel-selection telemetry for model families (7 days)
Phase 3: Full rollout with opt-out flag in tenant config and documentation (2 weeks)
Rollback: Automatic rollback if p99 increases >15% over baseline for >30 minutes
